questions.literal_question: What counts as one colony, can several players have colonies on one planet, and do five foreign colonies have to be in different systems?
questions.rulebook_material_asked: One colony per color per planet, coexisting colors, and five foreign planets need not span different systems.

source_references.section: Game Overview; What is a Colony?

questions.literal_question: At the start of an encounter, must the offense retrieve a warp ship if available, and where does the original rulebook place it when the offense has colonies or has none?
questions.rulebook_material_asked: Regroup retrieves one available offense ship to its colony, or directly to the gate without colonies; original-rulebook placement is the expressly asked source.

source_references.section: 1. Regroup

questions.literal_question: What happens when destiny has only one card left, and what choices does drawing your own color offer if your home system contains a foreign colony or a completely empty planet?

source_references.section: 2. Destiny; color, wild, special and hazard branches

questions.literal_question: Without a special power, may offense attack Blue’s foreign colony in Red’s home system after drawing Blue, and who defends Red’s empty home planet if foreign bystanders are present?
questions.rulebook_material_asked: Ordinary attacks do not reach another player's colony in a third player's system; the home-system owner defends at zero ships and foreign bystanders are not involved.

source_references.section: Can Macron Attack Clone's Colony in Zombie's System?; Defending with Nothing?; Bystanders

questions.literal_question: From where and how many ships may the offense launch, may it strip a colony, and can the defense move ships onto or off the targeted planet during Launch?
questions.rulebook_material_asked: One to four ships from any home/foreign colonies; last ship may be removed with immediate colony loss; defense cannot change targeted-planet ships.

source_references.section: 3. Launch
Stripping a Planet of Ships

questions.literal_question: In what order are allies invited and committed, can someone invited by both sides join both, and where do defensive allies put their ships?
questions.rulebook_material_asked: Offense invites first, defense second; clockwise commitments starting left of offense; one side only; defensive allies beside target.

source_references.section: 4. Alliance

questions.literal_question: An attacking side has an attack 10 and six ships; defense has attack 12 and four ships. Who wins, and what happens to offense, offensive allies, defense, defensive allies and bystanders?
questions.rulebook_material_asked: 16 versus16 is a defensive tie win; offensive side goes to warp; defending colonies stay, defensive allies return and collect rewards, bystanders unaffected.
